query: For high-entropy alloys intended as intermediate materials in plasma-facing reactor components, what single intervention could improve heat-transfer capability while preserving structural integrity? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the expected outcome compared with current intermediate-layer performance, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding 5 at.% Cu to the equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy and aging to precipitate a Cu-rich phase will increase its heat-transfer capability via enhanced electron and phonon conduction paths, while preserving >90% of its room-temperature and high-temperature strength under reactor-relevant loading.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional arc-melted, homogenized equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi HEA with single-phase FCC microstructure, thermal conductivity ≈10 W/m·K at 700 °C, room-temperature yield strength ≈800 MPa, high-temperature (700 °C) yield strength ≈400 MPa.
generation.intervention: Alloying the base HEA with 5 at.% Cu (nominal composition Cr18Mn18Fe18Co18Ni18Cu10), followed by homogenization at 1100 °C for 12 h and aging at 700 °C for 10 h.
generation.conditions: Steady temperatures 600–800 °C, uniaxial tensile loading up to 80% of baseline yield strength, inert He atmosphere, thermal cycling between RT and 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Cu-rich precipitates (~50–150 nm) dispersed in the FCC matrix forming a semi-continuous network.
generation.mechanism: The Cu-rich precipitates act as high-conductivity conduits that increase electron and phonon transport through the matrix without interrupting the FCC lattice continuity responsible for mechanical strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermal conductivity at 700 °C increases by ~20% (to ~12 W/m·K); room-temperature yield strength decreases by <5% (remains ≥760 MPa); high-temperature (700 °C) yield strength remains ≥360 MPa (>90% of baseline).
generation.baseline: CrMnFeCoNi HEA: 10 W/m·K at 700 °C; RT yield 800 MPa; 700 °C yield 400 MPa.
generation.boundary: Valid for 600–800 °C in inert environments; above 800 °C or under oxidizing/plasma exposure, precipitate coarsening or oxidation may negate benefits.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate – extrapolated from Cu additions in other FCC HEAs but untested specifically under reactor-relevant conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce baseline CrMnFeCoNi and Cu-modified CrMnFeCoNiCu5 specimens, process identically; measure thermal conductivity via laser-flash at 600, 700, 800 °C; obtain tensile stress–strain at RT and 700 °C; characterize precipitates by TEM and phases by XRD.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Cu-modified alloy shows <10% conductivity increase at 700 °C or high-temperature yield strength <85% of baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
